CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: China should retaliate with measured tariffs on remaining US imports to signal resolve without full economic decoupling. Maintain willingness to negotiate but demonstrate that escalation carries costs for both sides. Use the dispute to accelerate domestic consumption and supply chain diversification away from US dependency.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to China is HIGH and approaching existential territory. The US has escalated tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods from 10% to 25% (May 10, 2019), and Trump has called for tariffs on 'essentially all remaining imports from China, valued at approximately $300 billion' (Reuters timeline). This means nearly all Chinese exports to the US face tariff barriers, directly threatening China's export-dependent growth model. The USC analysis notes the trade war threatens 'the most important and potentially profitable industries of the future' including AI, cloud computing, and green tech — sectors central to Made in China 2025. Senator Graham explicitly states the US strategy is 'to break the stranglehold China has on the supply chain' (Fox Business). China has already retaliated on $110 billion of US goods but has limited remaining US imports to target. However, capitulation would set a precedent for US coercion and undermine CCP legitimacy. Retaliation is necessary to maintain negotiating leverage and signal that China will not accept unilateral demands. The risk of further escalation is real — White House adviser Kudlow acknowledged 'both sides will suffer' — but China's position is strengthened by the fact that US consumers and businesses also bear costs, creating domestic political pressure on Trump. China should retaliate while keeping channels open for negotiation, as both Lighthizer/Mnuchin and Chinese officials have indicated willingness to continue talks.
key_factors: US tariffs on $200B of Chinese goods raised to 25% (May 2019)
Trump threatens tariffs on remaining ~$300B of Chinese imports
US strategy explicitly aims to break China's supply chain dominance
Trade war extends to future tech sectors (AI, cloud, green tech) central to Made in China 2025
China has already retaliated on $110B of US goods but has limited remaining imports to target
Both sides acknowledge mutual economic pain (Kudlow: 'both sides will suffer')
Negotiations ongoing but China reportedly backtracked on draft trade pact commitments
